tasks.prompt: Write Python function dedupe_last(xs) returning a list with only the last occurrence of each hashable value, in the order those last occurrences appear. Input may be empty. Return only executable Python code.

SQLite tables customers(id,name) and orders(id,customer_id,amount,status). Return each customer id and the sum of non-NULL amounts on paid orders, including customers with no paid orders as zero. Sort by customer id. Return only one SELECT statement.
A shipment has 8 boxes of 6 items. Three boxes lose 2 items each; two other boxes gain 1 item each. Return only JSON with integer keys initial, final, lost_net.

One worker starts at minute 0. Tasks A=2 min, B=3 min, C=1 min; B must finish before C. Tasks cannot overlap or be interrupted. Give the lexicographically smallest task order among schedules with earliest completion. Return only JSON with keys order (array of task names) and finish_minute (integer).

Write Python function compress_runs(xs) returning a list of (value,count) tuples for consecutive equal values. Equality uses ==, so values need not be hashable; preserve order. Examples: [1,1,2,1] -> [(1,2),(2,1),(1,1)] and [] -> []. Return only executable Python code.

Write Python function interval_subtract(base,cuts). base is one inclusive integer interval (lo,hi) with lo<=hi. cuts is a list of inclusive integer intervals, each with lo<=hi. Return sorted, disjoint tuples for integers in base not covered by any cut. Touching at an endpoint removes that endpoint; adjacent intervals with no shared integer are distinct. Return only executable Python code.

Write Python function topo_lex(nodes,edges). nodes is a list of distinct strings; edges contains (before,after) pairs whose endpoints are in nodes. Return the lexicographically smallest valid topological ordering as a list of strings. If there is any directed cycle, return []. Duplicate edges are allowed and have no extra effect. Return only executable Python code.

SQLite tables customers(id,name) and orders(id,customer_id,status,amount). Return customer id and total paid amount for every customer, including zero when no paid order exists. Ignore non-paid orders and NULL amounts. Sort by total descending, then customer id ascending. Return only one SELECT statement.

SQLite table events(user_id,day,kind). Return each day and the number of DISTINCT non-NULL users who have at least one login AND at least one purchase on that same day. Include days with zero such users. Sort by day ascending. Return only one SELECT statement.

SQLite table products(id,category,price). Return category and its second-highest DISTINCT non-NULL price. Omit categories with fewer than two distinct non-NULL prices. Sort by category ascending. Return only one SELECT statement.

A box has 5 type-A items and 7 type-B items. A randomly selected A is defective with probability 1/10; a randomly selected B is defective with probability 1/5. Select one item uniformly from the 12. Return only JSON with exact reduced-fraction strings p_defective and p_B_given_defective.

A tank starts with 480 L. During minutes 0 through 15, inflow is 16 L/min and a leak removes 2 L/min. During minutes 15 through 30, the inflow stops; a pump removes 11 L/min and the same leak removes 2 L/min. No capacity limit. Return only JSON with final_liters (integer) and average_net_liters_per_min (number over all 30 minutes).

One worker starts at minute 0 and cannot work during [3,4). Tasks A=2 min, B=3 min, C=1 min, D=2 min; A must finish before C, and both B and C must finish before D. Tasks cannot overlap or be interrupted. Find earliest completion; among optimal schedules choose the lexicographically smallest task order. Return only JSON with order as an array of task names, starts as an array of integer start minutes in that order, and finish_minute as an integer.

Choose whole items under 10 kg. A weighs 6 kg and scores 11; B weighs 5 and scores 9; C weighs 4 and scores 7; D weighs 3 and scores 6; E weighs 2 and scores 4. A and D cannot both be chosen. Maximize score, then choose the lexicographically smallest sorted item list if tied. Return only JSON with sorted items array, total_weight integer and score integer.

Audit this synthetic operation log. An operation succeeds if any SUCCESS line for that operation appears; RETRY and FAIL lines alone do not count. Duplicate lines do not change status. The report must list failed operation IDs in ascending order and the number of distinct successful operation IDs. Log: 09:00 op=k4 FAIL; 09:01 op=k2 SUCCESS; 09:02 op=k1 RETRY; 09:03 op=k3 FAIL; 09:04 op=k1 SUCCESS; 09:05 op=k4 RETRY; 09:06 op=k2 SUCCESS; 09:07 op=k5 FAIL; 09:08 op=k3 SUCCESS; 09:09 op=k5 RETRY; 09:10 op=k6 SUCCESS; 09:11 op=k4 SUCCESS; 09:12 op=k7 FAIL; 09:13 op=k7 RETRY. Return only JSON with failed_ids array and success_count integer.

Compute effective config using these scattered synthetic rules. Defaults: region=eu, retention_days=30, alert=on. Environment overrides defaults. A command-line flag overrides environment. Tenant policy may only reduce retention_days and may force alert=on; it cannot change region. Inputs: environment region=us, retention_days=20, alert=off; flags region=apac, retention_days=14; tenant retention_days=7, alert=on, region=sa. Return only JSON with region string, retention_days integer and alert string.
